title: Trump Winds Down the War He Started With Goals Unmet
partialText: While the president says the agreement with Iran would open the Strait of Hormuz and provide economic relief, the country’s nuclear program is still a subject for negotiation.

title: Israel Counts the Ways That Netanyahu’s Iran Strategy Failed
partialText: The U.S.-Iran framework agreement appears to omit some of the most important provisions that Israel wanted.

title: Frustrated by Courts, Trump Weighed Suspending a Constitutional Right
partialText: Secret memos show that the White House debated last year, to a greater degree than previously known, whether to limit habeas corpus rights for undocumented immigrants.

title: What Is Habeas Corpus, and Why Are Trump Officials Talking About Suspending It?
partialText: Administration officials have suggested suspending a legal principle that protects against unlawful detention, and struggled to accurately define it.

title: Kennedy Seeks to Expedite Appeal of Ruling That Blocked His Vaccine Policies
partialText: The health secretary is trying to restart the work of a panel that advises the government on vaccines, after a judge froze its decisions and prevented it from meeting.

title: Democrats Warn Trump Officials Not to Pursue Arch Project Without Congress
partialText: In a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and national parks officials, lawmakers said that members of the administration could face fines and even criminal prosecution.

title: The Best TV Shows of 2026, So Far
partialText: The first half of the year had few big, buzzy hits. But there were some nice surprises (“Widow’s Bay”) and returning favorites (“The Comeback”).

title: Gov. Gavin Newsom Says Trump Is Investigating Him and His Wife
partialText: Aides to Gov. Gavin Newsom of California say several people associated with the couple have been contacted by federal agents in the past week. He criticized the move as politically motivated.

title: The Pain of Caring for a Parent Who Abused You
partialText: The United States is reliant on unpaid family caregivers, and millions of adult children are caring for parents who didn’t really care for them.

title: Tensions Are Rising Between States That Rely on the Colorado River
partialText: A prolonged drought means the nation’s largest reservoirs are dwindling, and litigation over access to water could lie ahead.

title: A Bystander at a ‘No Kings’ March Was Killed. Did the Shooter Commit a Crime?
partialText: A gunman believed he was defending the crowd, then killed an innocent protester. The legal case is complicated.

title: SpaceX’s Stock Surges on First Full Day of Trading
partialText: The company’s shares jumped on Monday, and executives announced that they had raised even more money in an already record-breaking initial offering.

title: Will SpaceX Fortunes Trickle Down to This Texas Town?
partialText: Elon Musk built a huge complex outside the city of Bastrop, population 14,000. Its residents now wonder what the historic SpaceX initial public offering might mean for them.

title: Trump Marks 80th Birthday With a UFC Cage Match at the White House
partialText: President Trump sat ringside beside his wife, Melania Trump, for an event that used the trappings of the White House for a U.F.C. brawl.

title: The Look of Patriotism at Trump’s UFC Fight
partialText: From the athletes to the Octagon Girls, the Freedom 250 Flag Day event was a fashion show in red, white and blue.

title: N.Y. Officials Reject Students’ Pleas to Move Exams for Knicks Parade
partialText: The championship celebration starts at 10 a.m. Thursday, just as some of the state Regents tests begin. Students had organized petitions calling for the exams to be delayed.

title: Is This the End of Political Islam?
partialText: For decades, Islamic governance held allure in the Middle East. Now some scholars say the Islamist wave has passed.

title: If Democrats Want to Win the House, Their Battle May Start Here
partialText: A bitterly fought Democratic primary in New York’s Hudson Valley will determine who takes on Representative Mike Lawler, one of the more vulnerable Republicans this cycle.

title: Alabama’s Senate Primary Runoff Again Tests Trump’s Hold on G.O.P.
partialText: Representative Barry Moore, an early backer of the president during his first campaign, faces Jared Hudson, a former Navy SEAL tapping into the excitement for outsiders.

title: In Alabama, Opposition to Renewable Solar Energy Joins a Data Center Battle
partialText: Tuesday’s runoff for a slot on the Alabama Public Service Commission has a familiar ring to it, with talk of data centers and electricity costs. But in a southern twist, solar power has joined the list of villains.

title: Millions of Women Are Left Out of Menopause’s Moment
partialText: Women who can’t take hormone therapy because of breast cancer or other diseases say they are deeply frustrated.

title: One City Might Have Just Cracked the Housing Crisis
partialText: A large real estate development in the middle of Vancouver, British Columbia, shows how cities can build more housing.

title: The States Should Override Trump’s Indefensible Pardons
partialText: The states can hold guilty parties responsible when the federal government will not.

title: Inside Colombia’s Never-Ending Drug War
partialText: Ten years after a landmark peace deal, armed groups are wreaking deadly violence, blending jungle combat with new drone warfare.
